stem: A provider orders cystatin C with eGFR for a client whose very low muscle mass may make creatinine-based estimates less reliable. Why is cystatin C useful in this situation?

options.A: It provides an alternative index of glomerular filtration that is less tied to skeletal muscle mass than creatinine
options.B: It measures liver synthetic function rather than kidney filtration
options.C: It is useful only when muscle mass is normal
options.D: It is unrelated to glomerular filtration rate

rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories describes cystatin C as an index of GFR that can be useful when serum creatinine may be misleading, including in people with atypical muscle mass. Unlike creatinine, cystatin C production is not linked to skeletal muscle mass in the same way.
educational_objective: Explain why cystatin C can help assess GFR when creatinine is confounded by abnormal muscle mass.
source_document_title: Cystatin C with Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR), Serum (CSTCE)
source_locator: Useful For; Clinical/interpretive rationale for use when creatinine may be misleading
source_claim_supported: Supports cystatin C as an index of GFR especially when serum creatinine is misleading due to atypical muscle mass.
correction_summary: Retained the source construct but anchored it to a concrete low-muscle-mass scenario and avoided claiming cystatin C is universally more accurate.
audit_findings: A is the specific advantage in this scenario; B-D misstate the test's purpose.
